summary: Adds the Garmin loopback SSO sign-in, the DI OAuth2 exchange and pre-call refresh, an identity assertion that refuses a token from the wrong account, and a one-time migration of the pre-press token file. Wired from internal/cli/root.go: registerNovelCommand runs configureGarminAuth, which replaces the generated auth setup/status/logout and hides set-token; registerClientHook runs installGarminFreshToken, which refreshes an about-to-expire token before the first API call for CLI commands and for internal/mcp/tools.go, which calls cli.ApplyClientHooks on the client it builds directly; addNovelCommandIfAbsent registers auth login, the generator's own novel-command scaffold with its RunE implemented in place as its header invites. No generated code was edited. REPRINT NOTE: the SKILL.md '## Auth Setup' block and the README '## Authentication' section are generated bearer-token boilerplate that a reprint restores; listing them in files[] does NOT preserve them (verified by control regen). Re-apply the auth-login choreography to SKILL.md and README.md by hand after every reprint until the upstream SKILL.md template honours the scheme's x-auth-instructions. SIGN-OUT CONFIRMATION ORDERING (N131.4h, finding F13): the H1 confirmation now fires AFTER the sign-in page opens, not between the logout and the sign-in navigation. Asked at the earlier point it can only confirm the logout page, which reads "Logged out!" whether or not Garmin then re-fills the sign-in form from a surviving SSO session -- and that autofilled form is the exact failure H1 exists to catch. The order is now: open the CAS logout, bind the loopback listener, open the sign-in URL (which already carries the state nonce in its service/redirect parameters), then prompt "Does the Garmin page show an EMPTY sign-in form? [y/N]:". Answering anything but y/yes aborts immediately with the sign-out instruction and never waits for a callback; y falls through to the existing wait. The prompt is skipped, and the previous advisory line printed instead, when nobody can answer or nothing was signed out: --no-logout, --no-input (which --agent sets), --yes, or no terminal on both ends. Two package-level seams in auth_login.go make this testable without a browser: garminOpenURL (production: openSetupURL) and garminIsInteractive (production: garminInteractive, which insists on a char-device stdin a test cannot supply). PERSIST ORDER (N131.7.4, upstream PR review): step 6 is now garminPersistLoginResult(configPath, configFlag, tokens, identity), an unexported function a test can drive without the browser flow. It still runs under garminWithAuthLock and still does config.Load inside the lock, but the two writes swapped order. It used to call SaveTokens first and garminSaveIdentity second, so a sidecar failure reported a failed login over credentials that had already changed: the caller was told nothing was stored while the next command used the new token with no record of which account issued it. Now the sidecar's current raw bytes are held (absent is a valid state; any other read failure returns before anything is written), the new sidecar is written, and SaveTokens is the commit point. SaveTokens is itself two writes — credentials.toml in the data dir, then config.toml — so the rollback is conditional: garminCredentialsFingerprint digests the credential file before and after, and the sidecar is put back (or removed, when none existed) only when that digest is unchanged or unreadable. When the digest changed, the second write is what failed, the home already holds the new chain, and the new sidecar is left naming it while the error says so and points at auth status --verify / auth logout. A failed put-back wraps the original error with what is actually on disk now rather than claiming a clean failure. The sidecar holds no secret, so restoring it costs nothing, while the token chain is what an owner-gated browser login would be needed to recreate. Note what the order does NOT prove: the sidecar shares the config dir with config.toml, but SaveTokens writes credentials.toml into the DATA dir first (cliutil.SaveCredentials resolves through DataDir()) and config.toml second, so writing the sidecar first exercises the config dir, never the data dir. The guarantee is simply that a sidecar failure happens before any credential write at all.
reason: Garmin issues no personal API token, so the generated bearer-token contract (auth setup / auth set-token prose about pasting a key) describes a credential that does not exist. The spec declares a plain bearer scheme with no token_url, so the generator emitted no refreshAccessToken at all: without a hand-authored refresh the stored token dies after roughly 22 hours. The identity assertion exists because a browser that is already signed in to another household member's Garmin account silently returns that account's ticket, and nothing in the token itself names the account.
call_sites: func garminPersistLoginResult(configPath, configFlag string, tokens *garminTokens, id *garminIdentity) error {
validated_outcome: go build ./..., go vet ./... and the auth test set pass. Both household homes were migrated off the pre-press token file and then proved live: auth status reports the right home rung, auth status --verify confirms the account with one call to Garmin, and the generated `account personal-information` command returns the matching userInfo.email through the generated HTTP client. The two homes report different account ids, and the legacy-config parse warning is gone from both. ORDERING (N131.4h): three new tests in garmin_auth_test.go assert the SEQUENCE rather than co-occurrence, by appending logout / signin / prompt to one slice from both seams. TestLoginAsksAboutTheFormOnlyAfterTheSignInPageIsOpen also GETs the callback URL parsed out of the sign-in URL at the moment that page opens and requires the 204 the ticket-less handler path returns, proving the listener was already bound, and asserts the 32-hex state nonce is already in that URL; answering N returns immediately with an error naming the logout route rather than waiting out a one-hour timeout. TestLoginWaitsForTheCallbackAfterTheFormIsConfirmedEmpty answers y, drives a synthetic ticket into the loopback listener and asserts exactly one exchange against an httptest token service reached through GARMIN_TOKEN_URL. TestLoginDoesNotPromptWithoutSomeoneToAnswer covers the no-TTY and --no-logout paths: no prompt, the advisory line printed, and the flow still waits. No browser was opened and no Garmin host was contacted. PERSIST ORDER (N131.7.4): seven cases in internal/cli/auth_login_persist_test.go drive garminPersistLoginResult directly with a synthetic token chain, no browser and no Garmin host. The two that were RED before the reorder are the defect itself — with the sidecar path blocked, the failed login wrote a 173-byte credentials.toml, and with a credential already on disk it rewrote it with the second chain. Both now report the error with credentials absent, or byte-identical to before. The three regression guards: a credential failure with a prior sidecar restores it byte-for-byte (the file holds the prior account's email, not the one the failed login tried to write), a credential failure with no prior sidecar leaves none behind, and a clean run writes both with the sidecar round-tripping through garminLoadIdentity. The success case also pins where each file lands, by stat rather than by reading the code: the sidecar beside config.toml, the credential in <home>/data/credentials.toml, and nothing at Dir(config)/credentials.toml or Dir(config)/data/credentials.toml. Credential failures are induced with a regular file where the data dir's parent must be, and the prior-bytes read failure with a directory at the sidecar path; both fail for root, so those cases need no os.Geteuid() guard and no Windows skip. A directory at the sidecar path fails the READ, not the write, so two further cases drive the sidecar WRITE failure and the config.toml-only failure through the garminSaveIdentityForPersist seam — TestPersistLoginLeavesCredentialsUntouchedWhenTheSidecarWriteFails and TestPersistLoginTellsTheTruthWhenOnlyConfigTomlFails — and of those two only TestPersistLoginTellsTheTruthWhenOnlyConfigTomlFails carries the root and Windows skips, because the read-only directory is what it depends on; the sidecar-write case fails the seam with a synthetic error on every platform. Seven cases in all.
regen_notes: internal/cli/auth_login.go is the press's own novel-command scaffold with its RunE implemented in place, which `generate --force` preserves; it is not a generated render that a reprint rewrites. The risk a reprint carries here is losing the file, not silently reverting its body.

N131.7.4: the persist order lives in garminPersistLoginResult and garminRollbackIdentity (internal/cli/auth_login.go), and the sidecar write goes through the garminSaveIdentityForPersist seam so a test can fail it. Swapping the two writes back — SaveTokens before garminSaveIdentity — reddens TestPersistLoginLeavesCredentialsUntouchedWhenTheSidecarWriteFails ("a failed sidecar write let credentials through ... 173 bytes"); it does NOT redden the two cases that block the sidecar path on disk, because that blocks the prior-bytes READ, which returns before SaveTokens in either order. Dropping the rollback reddens TestPersistLoginRestoresThePriorSidecarWhenTheCredentialWriteFails and TestPersistLoginLeavesNoSidecarWhenTheCredentialWriteFailsAndNoneExisted; making the rollback unconditional again reddens TestPersistLoginTellsTheTruthWhenOnlyConfigTomlFails.

The prior-bytes read must keep absent (os.IsNotExist) separate from unreadable. Collapsing both to "absent" sends the rollback down the os.Remove branch, and os.Remove succeeds on an empty directory — which would quietly delete the very blocker TestPersistLoginLeavesCredentialsUntouchedWhenThePriorSidecarReadFails installs and turn it green for the wrong reason.
